newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called higher on IPE gains, heat oil.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called higher on IPE gains, heat oil.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called higher Friday tracking gains of Brent futures on London's IPE amid tightening cash supply of heating oil.
"We have strength in London and tightness in the (New York) harbor, but crude is leading gains right now," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Inc.

Crude was called 15 to 20 cents a barrel higher. Heating oil and gasoline were called up 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon. Sun Co said increased demand due to the lower temperatures has drained its heating oil inventories, and that it was unlikely to resume supplying to distributors until late next week.

Cold tempertures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United State have boosted heating oil prices all week and the National Weather Services expects below normal temperatures to persist into next week.
Still, heating oil supplies were in surplus overall in the region, according to the American Petroleum Institute which said heat stocks were 3.4 million barrels over a year ago.
May Brent on London's IPE was up 36 cents a barrel at $18.05.
On Thursday, May crude ended seven cents higher a barrel at $19.42.
May gasoline finished up 0.32 cent at 60.70 cents a gallon and May heating oil ended 0.52 cent up at 54.00 cents a gallon.

The oil complex has lost some support as Lake Maracaibo shipping pilots have agreed to drop a strike threat after the Venezuelan government agreed to tighten oil tanker draught limits on a channel that has seen three groundings in the past two months.
Some 70 percent of Venezuelan exports pass through the channel into the Venezuelan Gulf.

However, traders are keeping an eye on a strike by 300 Rotterdam workers which they said could affect refined product shipments in Europe if the strike expands. On Thursday, port officials said the port itself and individual companies were largely unaffected.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
